report.title: Inference Engineering Report
report.generated: Generated {when} by Inference Lab from recorded experiments.
report.methodology_body: Each benchmark streams requests to a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Warm-up requests are discarded. Each trial runs a closed loop at a fixed concurrency until the request count is reached. TTFT is measured on the wire at the first generated text; TPOT = (end-to-end - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1). Medians across trials are reported with min and max to show run-to-run spread.
report.no_measurements: No live-measured records were selected, so this report makes no performance claims.
report.warn.non_measured_provenance: At least one record is not a measurement; the comparison cannot support a claim.
report.warn.more_than_one_variable_chang: More than one variable changed; differences cannot be attributed to a single cause.
report.warn.no_variable_changed: No variable changed; any difference is run-to-run noise.
report.obs.change: {metric}: {baseline} -> {candidate} ({pct}%). The min-max ranges across trials do not overlap.
report.obs.noise: {metric}: {baseline} -> {candidate} ({pct}%). The min-max ranges across trials overlap, so this may be noise.
report.lim.few_trials: Fewer than 3 trials in at least one benchmark: spread estimates are weak.
report.lim.cpu_only: Measured without a GPU. Results do not predict GPU serving performance.
report.lim.random_model: lab/tiny-random has random weights and ~1M parameters. Timings show pipeline behaviour, not the behaviour of a production-size model.
report.lim.mini_server: The Inference Lab mini server processes one request at a time (no continuous batching). Concurrency results reflect queueing, not an optimized engine.
report.lim.single_machine: All measurements come from one machine at one point in time; background load was not controlled.
report.decision_note: The decision above is written by the experimenter. Inference Lab does not generate it.
report.excluded_body: These records are listed for completeness. They are not measurements and support no performance claim.
report.imported_body: These records were imported from files. Their schema is valid and their checksums match, which only shows the files were not edited after export. Anyone can write a record with matching checksums, so these numbers are not claimed as measurements; re-run them on this machine before relying on them.
report.lim.imported: Some records are imported: their origin, hardware and settings were not verified by this lab.
report.warn.imported_unverified: At least one record is imported and its origin is not verified; the comparison cannot support a claim on its own.
report.warn.unknown_model_revision: The model revision is unknown for at least one record, so the weights may not be identical.
report.warn.unknown_engine_version: The engine version is unknown for at least one record.
stuck.ev.elapsed: Running for {s}s of a {budget}s time budget.
stuck.ev.heartbeat: Last sign of life (log line or progress update) {s}s ago.
stuck.state.working: Working. It is still producing signs of life, so it is not stuck, even if it feels slow.
stuck.state.slow_no_progress: Still alive, but progress has not moved for a while.
stuck.state.possibly_stalled: No sign of life for a while. It may be stalled.
stuck.state.over_budget: This is taking longer than its time budget.
stuck.state.process_exited: The process stopped before becoming healthy.
stuck.cause.generic: The machine may be busy with other work, or a network or disk operation is slower than usual.
stuck.cause.model.download: Large files download slowly on a slow connection; a proxy or firewall can also silently block the transfer.
stuck.cause.server.start: Loading weights takes time; on a GPU, vLLM also profiles memory and captures CUDA graphs before /health answers. A crash during load also looks like waiting.
stuck.cause.bench.run: Under high concurrency each request waits in a queue; a very slow server can make a trial take much longer than expected.
stuck.cause.inference.run: The first load of a model reads all weights from disk; large models on CPU generate slowly.
stuck.next.wait: Keep waiting. You can watch the log stream to see what it is doing.
stuck.next.logs: Open the log stream and read the last lines. They usually name the slow step.
stuck.next.slow_no_progress: Compare the log to the expected output in this step. If nothing changes for several more minutes, check network/disk activity.
stuck.next.possibly_stalled: Check whether the process is still alive (Server health) and look for errors in the log tail.
stuck.next.over_budget: Decide whether to keep waiting or to stop and retry with a smaller model or fewer requests.
stuck.next.process_exited: Read the log tail: it usually contains the exact error (for example, out of memory or a missing file).
err.approval_required.what: Nothing ran. This action needs your explicit approval first.
err.approval_required.why: It can use significant network, disk, GPU time, or start a container.
err.approval_required.next: Read the command and the expected cost, then press Approve and run if you agree.
err.capability_missing.what: Not run: this machine lacks something the action needs.
err.capability_missing.why: The hardware scan did not find a required capability (for example an NVIDIA GPU, a running Docker daemon, PyTorch, or access to the Hugging Face Hub).
err.capability_missing.next: Re-run Meet Your Machine after installing the missing piece, or use the CPU path shown in this mission.
err.hub_unreachable.what: The Hugging Face Hub could not be reached.
err.hub_unreachable.why: No internet connection, a proxy/firewall that blocks huggingface.co, or a DNS problem. This is about the network, not the model.
err.hub_unreachable.next: Open https://huggingface.co in a browser from this machine. If you use a mirror, set HF_ENDPOINT before starting the lab.
err.not_found_or_private.what: The Hub has no public model with that id.
err.not_found_or_private.why: The id may be misspelled, the repo may be private, or it is gated and needs an access token.
err.not_found_or_private.next: Check the exact id on the model page (owner/name, case-sensitive). For gated models, accept the terms on the Hub and set HF_TOKEN.
err.hub_error.what: The Hub answered with an unexpected error.
err.not_a_hub_model.what: lab/tiny-random lives only on your machine.
err.not_a_hub_model.why: It was built locally, so the Hub has no page for it.
err.download_refused.why: The model needs remote code, is gated, or only ships pickle weights (.bin), which can execute code when loaded.
err.download_refused.next: Choose a model that ships .safetensors weights and needs no trust_remote_code.
err.download_too_large.what: Download refused: larger than the configured limit.
err.download_too_large.why: Large downloads cost time and disk. The default limit is 2 GiB.
err.download_too_large.next: Pick a smaller model, or raise INFERENCE_LAB_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES deliberately.
err.download_size_unknown.what: Download refused: the size is unknown.
err.download_size_unknown.why: The Hub did not report file sizes, so the lab cannot tell you what you are approving.
err.download_size_unknown.next: Inspect the model again, or download it yourself with huggingface-cli after checking the files.
err.model_not_local.what: The model is not on this machine yet.
err.model_not_local.why: Inference loads files with local_files_only=True; nothing is fetched implicitly.
err.model_not_local.next: Build lab/tiny-random, or approve a download in the Model Garage first.
err.remote_code_refused.why: Remote code is arbitrary Python from the model repository and runs with your permissions.
err.remote_code_refused.next: Review the code yourself and load it outside the lab if you decide to trust it.
err.server_not_healthy.what: The server did not become healthy.
err.server_not_healthy.why: It crashed while loading (often out of memory, a missing model, or a port already in use) or took longer than its time budget.
err.server_not_healthy.next: Read the log tail in this run. Try another port, a smaller model, or a lower --gpu-memory-utilization.
err.no_healthy_server.what: There is no healthy server to benchmark.
err.no_healthy_server.why: Benchmarks send HTTP requests to a running server.
err.all_requests_failed.why: The server may have crashed, rejected the request shape, or timed out.
err.all_requests_failed.next: Check Server health and its log, then retry with fewer requests.
err.benchmark_aborted.why: All warm-up requests failed, so the measured trials would only measure errors.
err.benchmark_aborted.next: Check Server health and send one request manually.
err.experiment_not_found.what: That experiment record does not exist.
err.experiment_not_found.why: The id may be wrong or the record was produced on another machine.
err.experiment_not_found.next: Pick ids from the Engineering Journal.
err.unexpected_error.why: This is likely a bug or an unusual environment. The full error is kept in the run record.
err.unexpected_error.next: Open the run's raw output, then report it with the error text.
err.timeout.what: The run hit its time limit and was stopped.
err.timeout.why: Each action has a deadline so a stuck step cannot hold resources forever. Work that cannot be interrupted (one generate call, a download in progress) may still finish in the background; its result is discarded.
err.timeout.next: Retry with a smaller model, fewer requests or fewer tokens. If it keeps happening, check Server health and the log tail.
err.cancelled.what: The run was stopped before it finished.
err.cancelled.why: You (or a client) asked to cancel it. Partial results are not saved as experiments.
err.cancelled.next: Start it again when you are ready.
err.too_many_runs.what: Nothing ran: too many runs are still active.
err.too_many_runs.why: The lab caps how many actions run at once (INFERENCE_LAB_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS) so repeated clicks cannot exhaust memory or CPU.
err.too_many_runs.next: Wait for a running action to finish, or cancel one, then try again.
tutor.no_curated_code: No curated explanation and no docstring for this code. Read it line by line, or configure an AI tutor provider.
tutor.docstring_note: This is the docstring from the actual source file, shown as written.
tutor.no_provider: No AI provider is configured, so here are curated explanations that match your question. Everything in the lab works without AI.
tutor.provider_failed: The AI provider did not answer. Showing curated explanations instead.
tutor.ai_warning: AI-generated explanation. It may be wrong. It never decides whether a step succeeded.
suggest.queueing_serial.evidence: Raising concurrency from {c1} to {c2} raised median TTFT by {ttft}% while output throughput changed by only {thr}%.
suggest.queueing_serial.cause: The mini server generates one request at a time, so extra concurrent requests wait in a queue. Waiting shows up as TTFT.
suggest.queueing_serial.change: Serve the model with an engine that batches concurrent requests (vLLM with continuous batching), or keep concurrency at the level where TTFT is acceptable.
suggest.queueing_serial.impact: With batching, throughput should rise with concurrency until the GPU saturates, and TTFT should grow much more slowly.
suggest.queueing_serial.drawbacks: vLLM needs an NVIDIA GPU and more memory; batching can slightly increase per-token latency (TPOT).
suggest.queueing_serial.validation: Re-run the same two benchmarks against the new engine, changing only the engine, and compare TTFT P50/P95 and throughput.
suggest.queueing_saturated.evidence: Raising concurrency from {c1} to {c2} raised median TTFT by {ttft}% while output throughput changed by only {thr}%.
suggest.queueing_saturated.cause: The server appears saturated: extra requests mostly wait instead of increasing the work done per second.
suggest.queueing_saturated.change: Find the knee: sweep concurrency in smaller steps and pick the highest value that meets your TTFT target.
suggest.queueing_saturated.impact: You get the best throughput that still meets your latency goal.
suggest.queueing_saturated.drawbacks: More benchmark runs; the knee shifts with prompt and output length.
suggest.queueing_saturated.validation: Plot TTFT P95 and throughput against concurrency and check that the chosen point meets the target in repeated trials.
suggest.batching_helps.evidence: Raising concurrency from {c1} to {c2} increased output throughput by {thr}% (TTFT changed by {ttft}%).
suggest.batching_helps.cause: The engine processes concurrent requests together, so the hardware does more useful work per step.
suggest.batching_helps.change: Try a higher concurrency to find where throughput stops growing.
suggest.batching_helps.drawbacks: Latency per request usually rises as batches grow.
suggest.batching_helps.validation: Sweep concurrency and keep every other variable fixed.
suggest.decode_bound.evidence: Changing max_tokens from {t1} to {t2} changed median end-to-end latency by {e2e}%.
suggest.decode_bound.cause: Generation happens one token at a time, so total latency grows roughly with the number of output tokens.
suggest.decode_bound.change: Limit output length where the product allows it, or stream tokens so users see progress early.
suggest.decode_bound.impact: Lower end-to-end latency; streaming improves perceived latency without changing total time.
suggest.decode_bound.drawbacks: Shorter answers may be less complete.
suggest.decode_bound.validation: Compare E2E P50 at the new limit with the baseline, all else equal.
suggest.errors_present.evidence: The candidate run had an error rate of {rate}%.
suggest.errors_present.cause: Timeouts or server errors under load. Latency numbers only describe the requests that succeeded.
suggest.errors_present.change: Fix the errors first (longer timeout, lower load, or more memory) before optimizing latency.
suggest.errors_present.impact: Results that describe all requests, not just the lucky ones.
suggest.errors_present.drawbacks: None; error-free runs are a precondition for fair comparison.
suggest.errors_present.validation: Re-run until the error rate is 0 in every trial.
suggest.confounded.evidence: These variables differ between the two runs: {vars}.
suggest.confounded.cause: With more than one change, you cannot tell which one caused the difference.
suggest.confounded.change: Re-run the candidate changing only one variable compared with the baseline.
suggest.confounded.impact: A difference you can attribute to a single cause.
suggest.confounded.validation: The comparison should list exactly one changed variable.
